stories.title: Democratic Governors-Backed Super PAC Puts $4.3 Million Behind Hochul
stories.dek: A super PAC backed by the Democratic Governors Association has spent $4.3 million supporting Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection bid against Republican Bruce Blakeman.
body: Greater Empire State, a super PAC backed by the Democratic Governors Association, has put $4.3 million behind Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection campaign, according to Hoodline, which cited reporting by the New York Post. The group's first general-election television ads, which ran Saturday, cast Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman as aligned with President Trump's agenda.

State filings show the PAC raised about $4.34 million between late July and Oct. 2, Hoodline reported. Listed donors include former Mayor Michael Bloomberg and the Greater New York Hospital Association Management Corp., at $1 million each, a $1 million transfer from the super PAC Leadership for New York, and $600,000 from the Sports Betting Alliance.

According to Newsday, as cited by Hoodline, the association entered the 2022 race less than a week before Election Day, while this year's PAC launched in the summer. The state Democratic Committee separately gave Hochul's campaign $10 million in September. A pro-Blakeman super PAC has been spending $750,000 a week on TV ads attacking a COVID-19 testing contract awarded under Hochul, Hoodline reported.

Hochul's campaign declined to comment on the spending, according to the Post. A Blakeman spokesperson said the late money reflects Democratic desperation and that voters are ready to reject Hochul over taxes and utility bills.

Polls cited in the report differ. An October Marist poll of registered voters found Hochul ahead 53 percent to 42 percent, while a Pollfinity survey released Tuesday showed Blakeman trailing by 3 points.

sources.title: Democratic Governors Group Drops $4.3M to Shield Hochul From Blakeman Surge

stories.title: Police Search for Gunman After Fatal Shooting on Midtown Subway Platform
stories.dek: A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot and killed Saturday on an E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station, and police have released images of a man they are seeking.
body: A 26-year-old man from the Bronx was fatally shot Saturday afternoon on a Midtown subway platform, and police are still looking for the gunman, NY1 reported.

The man was shot once in the chest at about 12:20 p.m. on the northbound E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street, according to police. He was taken to Bellevue Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Investigators said the shooting followed an argument between two men.

Police released surveillance images of a man wanted in connection with the killing. He was last seen wearing a red tracksuit, a black vest and a black face mask and carrying a backpack, police said. No arrest had been announced as of Sunday evening, according to NY1.

MTA Chief Security Officer Michael Kemper said the agency is working with police and reviewing camera footage from the platform and train cars. He said guns have no place in the transit system. An MTA spokesperson declined to comment Sunday, and the NYPD did not respond to NY1's request for comment on a possible face-covering ban.

On Sunday, the rider advocacy group Passengers United gathered at the station to call for a ban on face masks in the transit system. Its president, Charlton D'Souza, argued that masks make it harder for police to identify suspects. Riders who spoke to NY1 said the killing left them feeling unsafe.
Anyone with information is asked to call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: NYPD searches for gunman in fatal Midtown subway shooting

stories.title: Mahmoud Khalil Asks Supreme Court to Let Judges Review Immigration Detentions
stories.dek: The activist and former Columbia University graduate student is appealing a ruling that federal courts cannot review detentions until immigration courts finish a case.
body: Activist Mahmoud Khalil asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Monday to let federal judges quickly decide whether immigration detentions are lawful, so that people are not held for months or years without judicial review, the Associated Press reported in a story published by NY1.

In court papers, Khalil asked the justices to overturn a ruling issued earlier this year by the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Philadelphia. That court found federal courts lack jurisdiction to review a detention's legality until immigration courts have fully considered the case, according to the AP.

Khalil, a lawful permanent resident and former Columbia University graduate student, was detained by immigration authorities in 2025 over his participation in pro-Palestinian demonstrations at Columbia in spring 2024. The government argued at the time that his presence harmed U.S. foreign policy interests. He spent more than three months in detention before a federal judge in New Jersey ordered his release, finding the government had acted unconstitutionally, the AP reported.
The Department of Homeland Security said Monday that the administration acted within its legal authority and urged Khalil to self-deport using the CBP Home app.

The 3rd Circuit has stayed its ruling while Khalil appeals, and he remains free. The government has separately asked the Supreme Court to overturn a conflicting 4th Circuit decision that upheld the release of Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri. According to the AP, conflicting appellate rulings can make it more likely the court takes up a case; if it does, arguments would likely be heard next year.

sources.title: Activist Mahmoud Khalil asks Supreme Court to let U.S. judges quickly reverse immigration detentions

stories.title: City's Free 2-K Program to Expand to All Five Boroughs Next Fall
stories.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Gov. Kathy Hochul said more than 12,000 children will have access to free 2-K, up from about 2,000 seats this year.
body: New York City's free 2-K program for 2-year-olds will expand to all five boroughs next fall, including every school district in the Bronx and on Staten Island, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Monday, NY1 reported.

More than 12,000 children will have access to the program, up from roughly 2,000 who received seats in this year's initial rollout, Mamdani said at a news conference. Once the expansion takes effect, 22 of the city's 32 school districts will take part, according to NY1. The mayor said the program will save parents more than $25,000 per child per year.

According to the mayor's office, the expansion adds seats in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens and increases capacity in the five districts where 2-K launched: District 6 in Manhattan, District 10 in the Bronx, Districts 18 and 23 in Brooklyn and District 27 in Queens. New districts include Districts 4 and 5 in Manhattan; Districts 16, 17, 19, 20, 21 and 32 in Brooklyn; and Districts 24, 28 and 29 in Queens.
Mamdani said families across the city would feel relief when placements are announced next year and that the city should stay affordable for people raising children.

The expansion is part of the administration's broader push on child care. Earlier this month, the city moved more than 10,000 children off a waitlist for free child care vouchers, NY1 reported. The city said it will release details on the 2-K application timeline in the coming weeks.

sources.title: New York City's 2-K program to expand to every borough next fall

stories.title: Wrong-Way Crash on Staten Island's West Shore Expressway Kills One, Injures Four
stories.dek: A 66-year-old driver died after her car struck a Range Rover traveling the wrong way on the West Shore Expressway, police said.
body: One person was killed and four others were hospitalized after a wrong-way driver set off a three-car crash on Staten Island's West Shore Expressway on Saturday morning, police said, according to Hoodline.

A Range Rover heading north ended up in the southbound lanes, where a southbound Kia Seltos driven by a 66-year-old woman struck it, according to the report. A southbound Jeep driven by a 21-year-old woman then hit both vehicles.

The 66-year-old Kia driver was pronounced dead at the scene. The Jeep driver, the 36-year-old woman driving the Range Rover and two passengers in the Jeep were taken to Richmond University Medical Center, where they were listed in stable condition, Hoodline reported, citing ABC7.
All of the drivers remained at the scene. The NYPD Collision Investigation Squad is investigating, no arrests have been made and police have not announced a cause.

Hoodline noted that wrong-way crashes caused 704 deaths nationwide in 2022, up from 445 in 2018, according to Federal Highway Administration figures. The same expressway was the site of a fatal wrong-way crash in 2015.

sources.title: Wrong-Way Driver Dead, Four Hurt in Staten Island Expressway Pileup

stories.title: Mamdani Replaces Four Members of NYPD Civilian Complaint Review Board
stories.dek: The mayor named four new appointees to the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the independent agency that investigates police misconduct complaints.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Monday that he is replacing four of his five appointees to the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the city agency that investigates complaints of police misconduct and recommends discipline, amNewYork reported.

The new members are Reginald Greene, Lisa Hoyes, Lisa Landau and Wesner Pierre, according to amNY. Their backgrounds include criminal prosecution in the Manhattan District Attorney's Office, federal public defense, health law and youth violence prevention work. They replace John Siegal, Pat Smith, Sherene Crawford and Rahul Agarwal, changes City Hall confirmed to the outlet. June Northern, appointed by former Mayor Eric Adams in 2023, remains on the board, which also includes members chosen by the City Council, the public advocate and the police commissioner.

In a statement, Mamdani said public safety depends on accountability and that the new members would strengthen public trust. CCRB Chair Jennifer Jones Austin, whom Mamdani named the board's first permanent chair in nearly six years in July, welcomed the appointees and thanked the departing members.

The appointments follow Mamdani's announcement earlier this month of the NYPD's first comprehensive review of its use-of-force policies in a decade. That review came after an officer involved in a fatal 2024 police shooting in Queens retired with a disability pension before facing a disciplinary trial; Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch apologized for the department's failure to notify the CCRB, amNY reported.

Police unions criticized the moves. PBA President Patrick Hendry called for a review of how the CCRB interprets use-of-force policies, and Detectives' Endowment Association President Scott Munro accused the mayor of empowering a board he called anti-police.

sources.title: Mamdani replaces four members of NYPD civilian watchdog board amid broader accountability push

stories.title: Blakeman Says Hochul Takes Orders From Mamdani in Closing Pitch
stories.dek: Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman attacked Gov. Kathy Hochul's ties to Mayor Zohran Mamdani in an interview focused on public safety, taxes and utility costs.
body: Republican gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman said Gov. Kathy Hochul takes orders from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling her a "useful tool" of what he described as an anti-American movement in the Democratic Party, Hoodline reported, citing a New York Post interview.

Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, made the remarks in a 20-minute interview framed as a closing argument on public safety, taxes and utility costs, with just over two weeks left before the Nov. 3 election. Early voting begins Oct. 24.

The attack followed a campaign video Mamdani released Oct. 15 backing Hochul, in which the mayor criticized Blakeman on Medicaid, child care and cooperation with ICE, according to amNY. The video cited a past Blakeman pledge to cut Medicaid spending in half; at the Oct. 13 debate, Blakeman said he never made that statement. He said he supports universal child care for working parents but questioned paying for care for people who do not work.

In the interview, Blakeman said he would cut income taxes, end green-energy policies to expand energy supply including natural gas, and seek to cut utility bills in half, Hoodline reported. He also said he would push to end congestion pricing and fill NYPD vacancies. He has previously described plans for surveillance cameras, license-plate readers and facial-recognition technology along the Nassau-New York City border, according to Newsday.
Blakeman disputed polls showing him behind, calling the race close. Mamdani told amNY he expects to campaign alongside Hochul before Election Day.

sources.title: Blakeman Calls Hochul a 'Useful Tool' Who Takes Orders From Mamdani

stories.title: 1tbsp Plays All-Night Set at Nowadays on Oct. 22
stories.dek: The Brisbane-born dance project 1tbsp will play a sold-out all-night set at the Ridgewood club Nowadays on Thursday, Oct. 22.
body: Nowadays will hand its decks to 1tbsp for an all-night set on Thursday, Oct. 22, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The party runs from 9 p.m. to 3 a.m. at the club at 56-06 Cooper Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens.

According to the listing, 1tbsp is the touring dance project of a Grammy-nominated songwriter and producer from Brisbane, Australia, who also records as Golden Vessel. The listing describes the project's sound as indie-house and dance music that mixes warmth, leftfield ideas and pop melody, and says it grew out of parties the artist first ran in Brisbane.

Tickets started at $20 and are listed as sold out, with a resale queue active and online purchases limited to four per person. The event is 21 and over. Nowadays says it sometimes holds tickets back for the door, but entry without a ticket is not guaranteed and admission is at staff discretion.

The club's listing says harassment, violence and discriminatory behavior are not tolerated. For accessibility, wheelchair access is through the driveway, which is locked during parties, so guests are asked to check with staff at the street entrance. Bathrooms are gender-neutral, with one accessible indoor stall, and the booths, deck and backyard offer quieter spaces. The club notes that its parties typically use strobe lights and water-based haze.

sources.title: 1tbsp All Night at Nowadays, New York City

stories.title: Nowadays Nonstop Runs Overnight Oct. 24 With Ayesha, Mor Elian and Pearson Sound
stories.dek: The Ridgewood club's Nonstop party starts at 10 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 24, and runs until 3 p.m. the next day.
body: Nowadays will host its Nonstop marathon party starting at 10 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 24, and running until 3 p.m. Sunday, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The club is at 56-06 Cooper Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens.

The listed schedule opens with Arthur from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m., followed by Tasha until 3 a.m., The Untouchables until 5 a.m., BEARCAT until 7 a.m. and Baby Leo until 9 a.m. Ayesha and Mor Elian then play back to back until noon, and Pearson Sound closes from noon to 3 p.m. The listing tags the night as drum and bass and bass music, with sets ranging from dub and hardgroove to jungle and faster styles.

Tickets are listed from $25. RSVPs cost $10 before 11 p.m. and $15 before midnight, cover one person each and do not guarantee entry, according to the listing. Tickets are assigned by entry window, re-entry depends on capacity and online purchases are capped at four per person. The event is 21 and over.

Attendees can also access the Mister Sunday party in the club's backyard starting at 3 p.m., the listing says. Nowadays lists a safer-space policy, gender-neutral bathrooms with one accessible indoor stall and wheelchair access through the driveway.

sources.title: Nonstop: Ayesha, Mor Elian, Baby Leo, BEARCAT, Pearson Sound, Tasha, The Untouchables + more

stories.title: Mister Sunday Hosts Floating Points and Justin Carter at Nowadays Oct. 25
stories.dek: Floating Points joins resident Justin Carter for the daytime party's second-to-last session of the season in Ridgewood.
body: Floating Points will join resident Justin Carter at Mister Sunday on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Nowadays in Ridgewood, Queens, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The listing describes the party as the penultimate one of the season.

According to the listed schedule, Carter plays from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., Floating Points follows from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., and the two close the day playing back to back from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m. The party is held at the club at 56-06 Cooper Ave., and doors close at 8:30 p.m. The listing calls Floating Points a long-time friend of the party. The event is presented by Mister Sunday and Nowadays.

The listing does not state a base ticket price. RSVP holders receive $10 off the door charge before 4 p.m. and $5 off before 5 p.m., with RSVPs closing an hour before the party begins. Early-entry tickets are valid from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m.; after that, entry depends on capacity, according to the listing.

Organizers ask attendees to put their phones away and dance. The listing says the outdoor space offers both sun and shade, along with Mexican food, free water and alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks. Organizers also offer a contact option for people facing financial hardship who need help getting in, and the listing sets out a conduct policy against violence, harassment and discrimination.

sources.title: Mister Sunday: Floating Points and Justin Carter at Nowadays, New York City

stories.title: Hercules & Love Affair, Dustin Zahn and Eli Escobar Play Basement Oct. 24
stories.dek: The Maspeth club's sold-out Saturday lineup splits techno and house acts across its Basement and Studio rooms.
body: Basement, the club at 52-19 Flushing Ave. in Maspeth, Queens, has a two-room lineup on Saturday, Oct. 24, running from 10:30 p.m. to 7 a.m., according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The event is listed as sold out, with a resale queue active, and is 21 and over.

The main Basement room features Dustin Zahn, whom the listing describes as a veteran Midwest techno DJ returning to the club; Kameliia, a Bulgarian-born DJ and producer coming back after debuting there in April; and Ade Kassim, a New York artist making his debut with a mix of techno and sound art.

In the Studio room, Hercules & Love Affair headline with a set the listing says draws on classic house music. They are joined by Eli Escobar, a selector and member of Tiki Disco, and Andi, the founder of Synthecide, whose sets focus on 1980s dance, goth, industrial and pop, according to the listing.

The club's house rules prohibit photos and videos and phone use on the dance floor, require consent, and bar discrimination of any kind, the listing says. About 1,400 people had marked interest in the event on Resident Advisor.

sources.title: Dustin Zahn / Kameliia / Ade Kassim / Hercules & Love Affair / Eli Escobar / Andi at BASEMENT, New York City

stories.title: FIST Party Takes Over Basement in Maspeth on Oct. 23
stories.dek: Techno producer Lacchesi headlines the FIST party at Basement on Friday, Oct. 23, with a second lineup in the club's Studio room.
body: The FIST party comes to Basement, at 52-19 Flushing Ave. in Maspeth, Queens, on Friday, Oct. 23, running from 10:30 p.m. to 7 a.m., according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The night is presented by FIST and Basement and is 21 and over.

Lacchesi headlines the main Basement room. The listing describes his techno as cinematic and slow-building, with a hard edge tied to late-1990s classics. He is joined by Nene H, a Turkish-Azerbaijani artist whose 2026 release "Second Skin" the listing presents as a breakthrough, and by party residents Word of Command and DJ Clone.

The Studio room features Jubilee, a Florida-based label founder known for electro, grime and dancehall; Mez Monty, a Los Angeles house DJ whose sets feature diva vocals; and Connor Wrong, whose sets span psy, house, bass and grime, according to the listing.

Ticket prices were not shown on the listing. The club's house rules ban photos, videos and phone use on the dance floor, require consent and prohibit discrimination, with violators removed. The listing notes that buying a ticket does not guarantee admission. About 317 people had marked interest in the event.

sources.title: FIST: Lacchesi / Nene H / Word of Command / DJ Clone / Jubilee / Mez Monty / Connor Wrong at BASEMENT, New York City

stories.title: Ultra Naté Headlines Paradiso at Paragon in Brooklyn Oct. 23
stories.dek: Paragon's Paradiso night on Friday, Oct. 23, features Ultra Naté with Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash, Saia and RATONC1T0.
body: Ultra Naté will headline Paradiso at Paragon, the club at 990 Broadway in Brooklyn, on Friday, Oct. 23, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The night runs from 9:30 p.m. to 3 a.m.
The lineup also includes Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash, Saia and RATONC1T0, the listing shows. Resident Advisor tags the event as techno and house. The night is presented by Paragon.
Tickets are listed at $25 through Resident Advisor, and the event is 21 and over. About 149 users had marked interest in the event as of the listing.

In its event notes, Paragon advises guests to arrive early to avoid lines and to dress up, and says its ground floor is ADA compliant. The club's code of conduct prohibits racism, sexism, discrimination and violence, and asks guests to notify security if they witness harassment.
The listing did not indicate whether the event was close to selling out.

sources.title: Paradiso: Ultra Naté, Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash + Saia, RATONC1T0 at Paragon, New York City

stories.title: UK DJ Effy Plays H0L0 in Ridgewood on Oct. 23
stories.dek: The British producer and DJ Effy is the sole act on the bill at H0L0 on Friday, Oct. 23.
body: UK producer and DJ Effy will play H0L0, the club at 1090 Wyckoff Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens, on Friday, Oct. 23, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The night runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m., and Effy is the only act on the bill.

The event is presented by MeanRed Productions and H0L0 and is tagged as techno and tech house. It is 21 and over. Ticket prices were not displayed on the listing, which says group rates are available by contacting the promoter on social media. About 130 people had marked interest.

According to the listing's biography, Effy, whose name is Sophie Cooper, is a producer, DJ, radio host and label founder from the North West of England. She released her debut single in 2020 and has held a residency on Rinse FM. She has played clubs and festivals including Fabric, Parklife, The Warehouse Project and Amnesia in Ibiza, the listing says.

Her debut EP, Not What It Seems, came out in 2022 and was followed by tours of Australia, Japan and Europe. The listing also cites a Boiler Room set in Sydney and her track "iluv," released on Fragrance Recordings, the label she runs with Mall Grab. Her 2025 EP, The Syndicate, pays tribute to Blackpool and the North West, according to the listing.

sources.title: Effy at H0L0, New York City

stories.title: 'A Day in Tulum' Rooftop Party Comes to Superior Ingredients Oct. 25
stories.dek: Promoter Tropique stages a daytime rooftop music and arts event at the Williamsburg venue on Sunday, Oct. 25.
body: A daytime rooftop event billed as the A Day in Tulum Music and Arts Festival will take place at Superior Ingredients, 74 Wythe Ave. in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, on Sunday, Oct. 25, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. It runs from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m.

The event is presented by the promoter Tropique. According to the listing, it aims to recreate the experience of Tulum, Mexico, with house music, Mexican-inspired food, craft cocktails, art and live performances, set against the Manhattan skyline from the venue's rooftop.

The listed lineup includes FI-LO, Robidio, Kuff, Santo and Jason Merced, along with paired sets from Manuela and Its V1B3, and from Anthony Micele and Mike Tomlinson. Resident Advisor tags the music as minimal and Afro tech.

Admission is listed at $25, and the event is 21 and over. The listing does not show additional ticket tiers. As of the listing's last update, two Resident Advisor users had marked interest in the event.

sources.title: A Day In Tulum Music and Arts Festival at Superior Ingredients, New York City

stories.title: TWA Hotel Hosts Three-Day 'Mission: 60s' Space Event at JFK
stories.dek: The weekend event, running Oct. 23 through Oct. 25, brings former astronauts, an Apollo flight director and a Star Trek actor to the TWA Hotel.
body: The TWA Hotel at JFK Airport will host Mission: 60s, a three-day event focused on Apollo, aviation and 1960s space culture, from Friday, Oct. 23, through Sunday, Hoodline reported. Organizers say the event bridges the Apollo and Artemis eras of spaceflight.

The event is organized by Luna Replicas, which sells vintage space gear, and Space for Humanity, a nonprofit that funds spaceflight for people who are not professional astronauts, according to Hoodline.

Scheduled speakers include Apollo flight director Gerry Griffin, Time science editor Jeffrey Kluger, former NASA astronauts Nicole Stott and Ron Garan, Star Trek actor Bob Picardo and researcher Frank White. Weekend panels cover Apollo mission control, women in aerospace, lunar communications, science fiction and space advocacy. Uplift Aerospace will run a shared virtual reality experience for up to 50 people, and a Sunday keynote will focus on NASA's Artemis program.

Friday's program includes a guided trip to the 1964 World's Fair site in Flushing Meadows, where the New York Hall of Science's Rocket Park displays a Mercury-Atlas D, a Gemini-Titan II booster and a Saturn V F-1 engine. On Saturday, a gathering will be held aboard the hotel's restored 1958 Lockheed Constellation, which now serves as a cocktail lounge, with live music by Bonnie Gordon. A vendor hall runs both days.

A full-weekend pass costs $150 and single-day admission is $85, with add-ons for VIP access, galas and the Friday excursion, according to Hoodline. The hotel occupies Eero Saarinen's TWA Flight Center, which opened in 1962 and reopened as a hotel in 2019.

sources.title: TWA Hotel Goes Full Apollo Era With Three-Day Mission: 60s Space Bash

stories.title: Venetian Wine Bar Bicchiere Opens Second Upper East Side Location
stories.dek: Bicchiere, a wine and pasta bar serving house-made bigoli and Venetian small plates, has opened in a former Madame Bonté café space.
body: Bicchiere, a Venetian-style wine and pasta bar, has opened its second location on the Upper East Side, Hoodline reported, citing the neighborhood news site Upper East Site.

The new restaurant occupies a fully renovated storefront that previously housed a Madame Bonté café, according to the reports. Hoodline did not publish a street address, though the Upper East Site report it linked to refers to 84th Street.

The menu centers on fresh-made bigoli, a long extruded pasta, along with Venetian small plates. According to a review by The Infatuation cited by Hoodline, the bigoli is offered in seven preparations, and dishes include smoked salmon tarama and meatballs in marinara. The Infatuation describes the restaurant as a Northern Italian spot specializing in cicchetti, the small plates typical of Venetian wine bars.

A report from Prism News, also cited by Hoodline, said Bicchiere comes from the team behind Madame Bonté, a Parisian-style café group with three Upper East Side locations. Hoodline cited that report as its only source for the connection. The restaurant's hours and prices were not included in the report.

sources.title: Bicchiere Pours Into Former Madame Bonte Café Spot on Upper East Side

stories.title: Greenpoint Luxury Tower Ran on Generator Power for a Month After Fire; Tenants Sue
stories.dek: The Greenpoint, a 463-unit rental tower in Brooklyn, relied on a generator for more than a month after a Sept. 6 electrical fire, and tenants have filed housing court cases.
body: The Greenpoint, a 40-story, 463-unit luxury rental tower at 21 India St. in Brooklyn, ran on generator power for more than a month after an electrical fire knocked it off the grid, Hoodline reported, citing reporting by Gothamist.

The fire broke out around 8 p.m. on Sept. 6 and was put out by the FDNY just over an hour later, according to Gothamist. An email reviewed by the outlet indicated it started in an eighth-floor electrical closet. Building manager Rose Associates reconnected the electrical system and shut off the generator late on Oct. 7.

Residents filed 272 complaints about hot water and power outages over the past two years, 191 of them since the fire, and the city's Department of Housing Preservation and Development has issued 38 violations against the building since the fire, Gothamist reported. One resident said smoke alarms did not go off and that management did not explain the cause until the next day. Units rent for up to $12,000 a month.

A Rose Associates spokesperson said generator power kept all building services running, attributed the disruptions to an electrical malfunction in a building riser, and said the company followed city rules in restoring power.

Tenants have formed an association, and more than 110 residents signed demands for a full life-safety inspection. One tenant filed a case in Brooklyn housing court on Oct. 7 seeking a building-wide city inspection, and another tenant separately sued the owner, 19 India Fee Owner LLC, according to the report.

sources.title: Greenpoint Luxury Tower Ran on Generator for a Month, Tenants Sue Over Fire Fallout

stories.title: MTA Inspector General Finds Dangerous Roof Damage at Two Bronx Subway Shops
stories.dek: A report found water leaked onto a crane's electrical system for about 15 years at the East 180th Street shop and concrete fell inside the 240th Street shop.
body: The roofs at two Bronx subway maintenance shops are dangerously compromised after years of unaddressed repair requests, according to a report by the MTA Office of the Inspector General, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Daily News.

At the East 180th Street Yard Maintenance Shop, which maintains cars for the 2 and 5 trains, plants grow from roof cracks and rainwater has leaked into the electrical distribution room, the report found. Water dripped from the roof onto a crane's high-voltage electrical system for about 15 years, making the crane unsafe in wet weather and delaying some repairs. A former shop head told investigators the roof looked nearly the same in 2014.

At the 240th Street Yard Maintenance Shop, which services 1 train cars, water intrusion has caused chunks of reinforced concrete to fall into the shop, according to the report. NYC Transit's car equipment division has proposed replacing that roof several times since 1984. Investigators also found the MTA's capital plan did not always reflect actual conditions and that staff inspected structures without specialized training.

The MTA has emergency repairs underway and has made temporary fixes at both shops, according to Hoodline. The agency agreed with all of the inspector general's recommendations, including better inspections and trained assessors. NYC Transit has created a facilities division whose roof team has completed seven repairs so far.

Both shops are slated for major overhauls under the MTA's 2025-2029 capital program. Transit officials told WNYC the shops must be rebuilt before the agency can replace the aging R62 subway cars on the 1 and 3 lines.

sources.title: Bronx Subway Shop Roofs Endanger Crews; E. 180th St. Crane Leak Lasted 15 Years

stories.title: One Dead, One Injured in Park Hill Avenue Apartment Fire on Staten Island
stories.dek: A Saturday-night fire in a six-story apartment building on Park Hill Avenue killed one person and injured another, the FDNY said.
body: One person was killed and another was injured when fire broke out in a six-story apartment building on Park Hill Avenue on Staten Island on Saturday night, according to the FDNY, Hoodline reported.

The fire was reported at about 8:08 p.m. on the building's second floor, on the stretch of Park Hill Avenue between Sobel Court and Roff Street, according to the report. The injured person was evaluated at the scene, and their condition was not known as of Saturday night, CBS News New York reported. The person who died had not been identified publicly.
No cause has been made public, according to Hoodline.

The block has seen several fires in recent years. In June, a fire on the fourth floor of a building at 140 Park Hill Ave. injured a civilian and seriously injured a firefighter, according to the Staten Island Advance. In May 2021, a fifth-floor fire a few doors from Saturday's scene injured a civilian and a police officer, according to NY Fire News.

The building is part of the federally subsidized Park Hill Apartments complex, which a joint venture of The Arker Companies, L+M Development Partners and LIHC Investment Group bought in December 2025 for $364.7 million, Hoodline previously reported. The sale followed nearly 2,000 resident complaints to the city over heat and hot water outages and was described as a recapitalization to fund repairs.
Citywide, 46 people died in fires from January through mid-May, up from 28 in the same period of 2025, an FDNY official told CBS News.

sources.title: One Dead, One Hurt in Park Hill Avenue Fire on a Block With a History of Blazes

stories.title: Queens Father Sues NYPD, Alleging Officers Struck Moped Carrying His Teenage Son
stories.dek: A federal lawsuit alleges a marked police vehicle crossed a double yellow line in Corona and swerved into a moped carrying a 14-year-old passenger.
body: A Queens father has filed a federal lawsuit in Brooklyn accusing NYPD officers of deliberately steering a marked police vehicle into a moped carrying his 14-year-old son in Corona, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Daily News.

The crash happened near 101st Street and Northern Boulevard, according to the suit. The teen was riding as a passenger in a group of mopeds that officers from the 115th Precinct and the Community Response Team were targeting in a joint operation that evening, the lawsuit says. It alleges a police car approaching from the opposite direction, with its lights and sirens off, crossed the double yellow line and swerved into the moped's path.

According to the suit, the teen was knocked unconscious and suffered a fractured femur and a head bruise. His father said the boy was handcuffed while injured and that officers later told him his son would not be charged. The handcuffs were removed after a CT scan, the lawsuit says.

The family's attorney, Jon Norinsberg, alleges the NYPD has an unwritten practice of using police vehicles to block or strike two-wheeled vehicles, which the department's Patrol Guide prohibits. The allegations have not been proven in court.

An NYPD spokesperson declined to say what officers were responding to or whether anyone was arrested, and said an internal investigation is ongoing. The city Law Department declined to comment, according to the report. In January 2025, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch tightened the department's vehicle pursuit policy.

sources.title: Queens Dad Sues NYPD, Says Cops Rammed Moped Carrying His 14-Year-Old Son

stories.title: Vacate Order Issued After SUV Crashes Into Howard Beach Pizzeria
stories.dek: City inspectors ordered New Park Pizzeria's building vacated after a BMW SUV struck its dining area Thursday, injuring two people, the FDNY said.
body: City inspectors issued a full vacate order for the building housing New Park Pizzeria on Cross Bay Boulevard in Howard Beach, Queens, after an SUV crashed into the restaurant Thursday afternoon, NY1 reported.

The BMW SUV struck a portion of the building used for dining shortly after 1 p.m. on Oct. 15, according to the FDNY. Two people were injured, the driver and a person inside the restaurant. Both were taken to Brookdale University Hospital Medical Center with injuries that were not life-threatening, the FDNY said.

The NYPD's Emergency Service Unit responded Thursday afternoon to remove the vehicle, according to NY1. By Friday morning, vacate orders were posted on the restaurant's door warning people not to enter, and green scaffolding had been put up around the damaged section of the building.
The cause of the crash was not reported. NY1 said it had contacted the Department of Buildings for comment.
In a social media post, the pizzeria said it is working to reopen as quickly as possible.

sources.title: Vacate order issued after crash at Howard Beach pizzeria

stories.title: Natalie Maines Criticizes Trump at Beacon Theatre Show; White House Responds
stories.dek: The Chicks singer contrasted President Trump with George W. Bush during an Oct. 12 concert, prompting a statement from a White House spokesman.
body: Natalie Maines of the Chicks criticized President Trump during the band's Oct. 12 concert at the Beacon Theatre on Manhattan's Upper West Side, and the White House responded with a statement attacking the singer, Hoodline reported.

During the show, Maines said she would now give former President George W. Bush a kiss and said she was ashamed of the current president, a reversal of her 2003 remark about Bush, according to the report. She also said she would never bow to critics who tell artists to stay out of politics. MassLive reported that the show included a montage about the backlash the band faced in 2003.

On Oct. 15, White House spokesman Davis Ingle issued a statement calling Maines a "despicable nobody" and accusing her of suffering from "Trump Derangement Syndrome," according to US Weekly, as cited by Hoodline. Ingle issued a similar statement in May after Maines criticized Trump on Instagram, Taste of Country reported.

In March 2003, days before the U.S. invasion of Iraq, Maines told a London audience the band was ashamed President Bush was from Texas, leading to radio bans and public protests against the group, TIME and MassLive reported.

The Beacon show was part of the Chicks' 20-date tour marking the 20th anniversary of the album Taking the Long Way, which won five Grammy Awards including Album of the Year. The tour began Sept. 30 in Detroit, and an expanded reissue of the album was released Oct. 2.

sources.title: Natalie Maines Mocks Trump at NYC Show, White House Fires Back With Insults

stories.title: Bloomberg-Funded Charter School PAC Launches Campaign Backing Hochul
stories.dek: New Yorkers for a Balanced Albany, a pro-charter super PAC that received $1.8 million from Michael Bloomberg this year, is spending seven figures to reelect Gov. Kathy Hochul.
body: A pro-charter school super PAC funded by former Mayor Michael Bloomberg is spending seven figures on a get-out-the-vote and media campaign to reelect Gov. Kathy Hochul, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Post, which first reported the plans.

Bloomberg has given $1.8 million this year to the group, New Yorkers for a Balanced Albany, according to the Post. The PAC is also backing seven moderate Democratic state Senate candidates in competitive districts on Long Island, in the Lower Hudson Valley and the Capital Region, and in southern Brooklyn and Staten Island.
A spokesperson for the group, Crystal McQueen-Taylor, said Hochul has stood up for students and families and that parents are now canvassing for her in Brooklyn, Harlem and the Bronx.

The PAC was created in 2014 by the pro-charter group StudentsFirstNY. According to City & State New York, as cited by Hoodline, it initially helped Senate Republicans hold the chamber before shifting after 2019 to backing pro-charter moderate Democrats. Bloomberg separately gave $1 million to the pro-Hochul Empire State PAC in September, and his representatives declined to say whether he would spend more.

The spending comes as Hochul announced New York would opt into a new federal tax credit scholarship program, which the state teachers union opposed. On the other side of the race, a super PAC backing Republican Bruce Blakeman, partly funded by James Dolan and Steve Wynn, launched a $750,000-a-week ad campaign this month. The election is Nov. 3.

sources.title: Bloomberg-Backed Charter PAC Pours $1.8M Into Hochul's Re-Election Push

stories.title: Lawyers Say ICE Officer Fired Into New Yorker's Car Without Identifying Himself
stories.dek: Attorneys for a 28-year-old man shot by an immigration officer in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 dispute federal officials' account that he drove at officers.
body: Lawyers for a 28-year-old man wounded by a federal immigration officer on Oct. 8 say the officer approached his car without identifying himself, smashed a window and fired several shots, one of which struck the man in the neck, the Associated Press reported in a story published by NY1.

In a petition filed in Brooklyn federal court seeking his release, Legal Aid Society attorneys said the man, who is from the Dominican Republic, had picked up his young son from school and was stopped near a fire hydrant looking for parking when masked, armed men approached. The son was in the back seat, the lawyers said.

Department of Homeland Security officials say officers fired only after the man drove into two government vehicles and accelerated toward other officers, and that they feared for their lives. A senior ICE official said the man had refused orders to exit the car. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officers did not know a child was in the vehicle. DHS said the incident is under investigation.

NYPD security footage released last week shows a man with a gun drawn striking the driver's window until it shatters before the car pulls away, according to the AP. The footage does not show the shooting. The car later came to rest against a concrete barrier, and the man was taken to a hospital.

He remains detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn and has not had surgery to remove the bullet, his lawyers said. The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to discuss his care but said it does not deny necessary treatment.

sources.title: Lawyers for New York man shot by ICE say officer fired into car without warning

stories.title: Mamdani Appears in Ad Backing Hochul's Reelection Bid
stories.dek: The mayor's ad for Gov. Kathy Hochul criticizes Republican Bruce Blakeman on federal spending cuts, ICE and universal child care.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani appears in a new ad supporting Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection campaign, released Thursday, NY1 reported.

In the ad, Mamdani says he is voting for Hochul because she is "the real deal for New Yorkers" and calls her Republican opponent, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, "a bad apple," according to NY1. The ad says Blakeman believes a trillion dollars in federal cuts did not go far enough and would rather direct money to ICE, and it says he opposes universal child care. It also highlights the mayor and governor's work together on the city budget and affordability.
In a statement to NY1, Blakeman said Hochul and Mamdani cannot be trusted. He said he supports universal child care for working parents but questioned paying for care for people who are not working.

The ad's release coincided with an event in East New York, where Hochul, Mamdani and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries opened new housing. The first phase of the Innovative Urban Village project brings 386 affordable units to the neighborhood, according to NY1. At the event, Hochul said Albany and the city are aligned on affordability through housing.
Mamdani is expected to campaign with Hochul in the city during the final weeks of the race, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Mamdani puts out ad supporting Hochul's reelection bid

stories.title: Queens Officials Renew Calls to Abolish ICE After Marble Hill Shooting
stories.dek: Democratic lawmakers in Queens called for ICE to be abolished after federal agents shot a 28-year-old man in Marble Hill, while a Republican council member defended the arrest.
body: Elected officials across Queens renewed calls to abolish U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after federal agents shot a 28-year-old man in his car in Marble Hill on Oct. 8, QNS reported. The man's young son was in the car at the time.

ICE and federal officials say the man refused an order to leave the vehicle and tried to use it against agents, a claim critics dispute, according to QNS. The NYPD said at least one agent fired seven shots, striking the man in the neck. A federal judge in Brooklyn has temporarily barred his deportation and ordered authorities to explain why he should not be released.

Assembly Member Jessica González-Rojas called the shooting terrifying and said she fears similar incidents in Corona, Elmhurst and Jackson Heights. She and Assembly member-elect Brian Romero said increased ICE activity has hurt local businesses, and alleged that some businesses had allowed agents to use their parking lots. Neither business named in the report responded to QNS.

Council Member Julie Won urged Mayor Zohran Mamdani to fire Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch after officers clashed with protesters, and to disband the NYPD's Strategic Response Group. Council Member Tiffany Cabán also called for abolishing ICE. Mamdani has said he has no plans to fire Tisch, citing record-low crime, a decision Gov. Kathy Hochul called smart.
Republican Council Member Joann Ariola dismissed the abolition push and said the arrest was justified, according to QNS.

sources.title: Queens electeds renew calls for ICE to be abolished in wake of Marble Hill shooting

stories.title: Hochul Backs Mamdani's Decision to Keep Tisch as Police Commissioner
stories.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul called it a smart decision for Mayor Zohran Mamdani to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite calls from the Democratic Socialists of America to fire her.
body: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Mayor Zohran Mamdani made a "smart decision" in refusing calls to fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch, amNewYork reported. Hochul spoke at an event in Jackson Heights, Queens.

Members of Mamdani's political base, including the city chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America, have called for Tisch's removal over the NYPD's response to the Oct. 8 shooting of a 28-year-old man by an ICE officer in Marble Hill, according to amNY. The DSA chapter alleged officers clashed violently with protesters after the shooting. Other critics alleged that the NYPD helped ICE leave a hospital with the man in custody, which they said violated the city's sanctuary laws.

Mamdani told reporters Tuesday that he has no plans to fire Tisch, citing record-low crime and her work rooting out corruption in the department's upper ranks. Hochul said she supports that decision, praised Tisch's leadership and pointed to a decline in crime, amNY reported. She called the matter closed.

Pressure from the left has continued. Congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier, whom Mamdani endorsed, alleged that officers shoved her to the ground during the protests and called for Tisch's removal. Seventeen socialist state lawmakers and Democratic nominees signed a letter calling for Tisch to be fired unless she disbands the NYPD's Strategic Response Group and ends alleged assistance to ICE.
The article did not include responses from the NYPD, Tisch or ICE. Tisch remained commissioner as of publication.

sources.title: 'Case closed': Hochul says Mamdani made 'smart decision' by refusing to fire Tisch amid DSA pressure

stories.title: Maduro Calls New Torture Allegations False in Manhattan Federal Court
stories.dek: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro twice declined to enter a plea to a rewritten indictment, and a judge entered a not guilty plea on his behalf.
body: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro told a Manhattan federal court Thursday that newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife, Cilia Flores, are false, the Associated Press reported in a story published by NY1.

The rewritten indictment expands earlier drug trafficking charges and accuses the couple of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of people, including three Americans, according to the AP. Prosecutors allege Maduro oversaw the system and personally recommended methods, and that Flores, a former attorney general, helped develop it and ordered the torture of specific people. The charges cover alleged conduct beginning in 2013.

Maduro twice declined to enter a plea, calling the charges false accusations and false testimony through an interpreter, and U.S. District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein entered a not guilty plea for him. Flores told the court she is innocent. Defense attorney Barry Pollack said Maduro denies the charges and looks forward to his day in court. Both are presumed innocent.

U.S. military forces took the couple from their home in Caracas in a nighttime raid in January, the AP reported. Earlier this year, they pleaded not guilty to charges of conspiring to send cocaine into the United States; their lawyers argue that case should be dismissed on head-of-state immunity grounds.
The judge set trial for June 14, 2027. The couple is scheduled to return to court for a pretrial hearing on Dec. 17.

sources.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro says new torture allegations are 'false'

stories.title: Comptroller Levine Walks Back Pledge to Buy Israel Bonds
stories.dek: City Comptroller Mark Levine says technical challenges and financial considerations mean the city will not invest pension money in Israel bonds for now.
body: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine is reversing his campaign pledge to invest city pension funds in Israel bonds, citing financial considerations, NY1 reported, based on an interview Levine gave to The New York Times published Oct. 14.

Levine told the Times the decision was not politically motivated, though he acknowledged struggling with it personally. He said he had always maintained the choice would rest on financial grounds alone, and that technical challenges and financial considerations mean the city cannot make the investment right now. Asked why he made the pledge, Levine said he did not have a full understanding of the financial picture at the time, according to the Times.

Levine had vowed during his campaign to buy Israel bonds after his predecessor, Brad Lander, declined to renew the city's investments in 2023. According to the Times, the bonds have returned around 5 percent on two- and three-year investments, while their ratings remain below early-2023 levels.
Some Jewish leaders in the city expressed disappointment, including former Comptroller Scott Stringer, who invested millions of dollars in Israel bonds during his tenure, NY1 reported.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a separate news conference that he supports the decision. He said the city does not buy bonds from any other sovereign nation and should not make an exception for Israel, while noting the decision belongs to the comptroller.

sources.title: NYC comptroller walks back pledge to buy Israel bonds

stories.title: Exhibit at City Reliquary Marks 50 Years of Manic Panic
stories.dek: A Williamsburg museum show traces how two Bronx sisters opened what NY1 calls the nation's first punk rock boutique in 1977.
body: A new exhibit at the City Reliquary Museum and Civic Organization in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, spotlights Tish and Snooky Bellomo, the Bronx sisters who founded Manic Panic, NY1 reported. The show, "Still Manic After All These Years: 50 Years of Manic Panic," runs through March 28.

The sisters opened the shop in 1977 on St. Mark's Place in the East Village, in what NY1 describes as the nation's first punk rock boutique. Their mother, Estelle, gave it the name Manic Panic. The store sold hair color, Tish's original designs, Snooky's knitted sweaters, records, posters and fanzines, according to NY1.

Curator Lee Berman assembled the exhibit from the sisters' archives, including photographs from before the shop opened and from their performances and bands. The sisters also sang in the early lineup of Blondie, and a pair of Debbie Harry's platform shoes is part of the show, NY1 reported.
Manic Panic has since grown into an international hair dye brand with more than 50 colors. Tish told NY1 that advisers had warned the sisters against expanding overseas, but they did it anyway.
Snooky said she was excited about the exhibit and loves the City Reliquary, and Tish said they knew they had to do the show as soon as they walked into the museum.

sources.title: 50 years of punk: Manic Panic founders spotlighted in new exhibit

stories.title: Mamdani Stands By NYPD Commissioner Amid Calls for Removal After ICE Shooting
stories.dek: The mayor said Jessica Tisch will remain police commissioner and announced a review of the 24 hours surrounding an ICE shooting in Marble Hill.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch will keep her job despite calls for her removal following an ICE shooting in Marble Hill, NY1 reported.

Mamdani said he kept Tisch, who stayed on after former Mayor Eric Adams left office in January, because of her record of rooting out corruption and lowering crime, and that he has no plans to change that, according to NY1. At a press conference, he said no one in his administration serves on a set timetable.

Federal immigration officers shot a man in Manhattan's Marble Hill neighborhood last week, setting off protests and criticism of the NYPD's response, NY1 reported. The NYPD was not involved in the shooting itself. Critics of Tisch include members of the Democratic Socialists of America, congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and Council Member Carmen de la Rosa, who represents the area where the shooting happened. De la Rosa said the mayor is wrong on the issue, questioned whether police were at the scene to pursue the shooter or to help ICE leave, and has called for disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group.

Mamdani announced a review of the 24 hours around the incident, covering the shooting, the police response, the protests and ICE's use of a private parking lot as a staging area. It will also examine what other tools the city can use to protect immigrants.

The NYPD said the Strategic Response Group did not respond to or interact with the protests. A department spokesperson said officers did respond to the shooting and took the wounded man to a hospital. NY1 said the DSA and Chevalier had not responded to requests for comment.

sources.title: Mamdani stands by NYPD commissioner amid calls for removal after ICE shooting

stories.title: Two Men Plead Not Guilty in Stabbing and Robbery of Off-Duty NYPD Detective
stories.dek: Sneider Mejia and Dangelo Caraballo face charges including attempted murder in the Oct. 2 attack on an off-duty detective in Norwood, the Bronx.
body: Two men accused of stabbing and robbing an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx pleaded not guilty Wednesday, News 12 reported.

Sneider Mejia, 24, and Dangelo Caraballo, 25, face charges including attempted murder, robbery and assault on a police officer, according to News 12. Prosecutors asked that both remain in custody, arguing they are flight risks. The judge ordered them held pending bail applications. Defense lawyers noted that family members were in court. Both men are presumed innocent.

The attack happened at about 1:44 p.m. on Oct. 2 near Rochambeau Avenue and East 208th Street in Norwood, police said. According to police, two men on a motorized bike approached the 33-year-old detective, who was off duty and on vacation, stabbed him several times, took a chain from his neck and rode off. He was treated at Jacobi Hospital and has since been released.

Police said the two suspects were later found hiding in a basement in Lynn, Massachusetts, and were brought back to New York. The Department of Homeland Security said both men are Dominican nationals living in the U.S. without legal status and have prior arrests in New York, News 12 reported.

Speaking to reporters Tuesday, the detective said he identified himself as a police officer in English and Spanish during the attack and chased the men for about five blocks before a bystander called 911. He said he is still recovering from his injuries.

sources.title: 2 men accused of stabbing off-duty NYPD detective plead not guilty in Bronx court

stories.title: Bronx Vigil Honors Young Mother Allegedly Pushed From Balcony
stories.dek: Community members and advocates gathered a week after investigators say a 23-year-old woman and her infant were pushed from a 15th-floor balcony by her ex-boyfriend.
body: Community members and advocates held a candlelight vigil in the Bronx on Tuesday night for a 23-year-old mother who investigators say was pushed from a high-rise balcony by her ex-boyfriend a week earlier, NY1 reported.

Investigators said the man pushed the woman and the couple's 8-month-old daughter off a 15th-floor balcony at a Bronx building, and officials said the woman was holding the child when she fell, according to NY1. Officials said the infant remained hospitalized in critical condition.

The ex-boyfriend, Angel Carrasco, faces several charges, including murder and attempted murder. Police sources told NY1 he had been taken to a hospital and had not yet been arraigned. He is presumed innocent.

Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson said the woman's mother and grandmother were at the hospital with the baby, and that the community takes the attack personally. Council Member Kevin Riley urged men to do more to stop violence against women and children.

Advocates said they hope the case raises awareness of domestic violence, including warning signs and how to seek help. Stephanie McGraw, founder of the domestic violence organization WARM, said neighbors should speak up when they hear yelling, screaming or breaking glass. October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and advocates have been canvassing the area to share information about resources for victims, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Bronx community holds vigil for young mother pushed off balcony last week

stories.title: Mayor and Council Speaker Agree to Ban Horse Carriages by 2028
stories.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Council Speaker Julie Menin reached a deal on legislation that would phase out horse-drawn carriages and retrain drivers.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and City Council Speaker Julie Menin have agreed to ban horse-drawn carriages in New York City, NY1 reported. The speaker's office announced Tuesday that the bill would go to a council vote the following week, and Menin said a majority of council members support it.

The legislation is named for an 18-year-old tourist who died in June after being thrown from a carriage in Central Park, according to NY1. It would train drivers for new jobs before a full ban takes effect in 2028 and retire the horses to sanctuaries. The city would have to prepare a worker transition plan by April 2027, including measures such as job fairs and counseling, and the bill says the city should consider compensation for medallion owners.

In a statement, Menin said the carriages are part of the city's history but have become a public safety liability in an increasingly busy Central Park. City Hall spokesperson Sneha Choudhary said the administration worked with the council, unions, drivers, animal welfare advocates and community leaders on what she called a just transition. The bill's sponsor, Council Member Christopher Marte, said the tourist's family is grateful it is nearing passage.

The Transport Workers Union, which represents carriage drivers, opposes the deal. TWU President John Samuelsen said the bill offers no meaningful economic relief for workers and urged the mayor not to support it. Christina Hansen of TWU Local 100 questioned how job counseling would help drivers who lose their income. Drivers would fight a shutdown in court, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Mayor and City Council speaker agree to ban horse carriages in NYC

stories.title: Off-Duty NYPD Detective Stabbed and Robbed in Norwood Speaks Publicly
stories.dek: The detective, attacked Oct. 2 in the Bronx while on vacation, described identifying himself as an officer and chasing his attackers.
body: An off-duty NYPD detective who was stabbed and robbed in the Bronx's Norwood neighborhood spoke to reporters Tuesday for the first time since the Oct. 2 attack, News 12 Bronx reported.

The detective said he was stabbed 10 times, according to News 12. Stitches were visible on his right arm and his left arm was in a cast; he said he needs surgery and is working to regain movement in his left hand. He had been on vacation at the time of the attack.

He said he told the attackers in English and Spanish that he was a police officer, but that they ignored him. Despite his injuries, he said, he chased them for about five blocks before asking a passerby for help, and that person called 911. He told News 12 that his police training made his response instinctive and that his main goal was to give responders a clear description of the suspects.

Two men, Dangelo Caraballo and Sneider Mejia, were arrested in Massachusetts and brought back to the Bronx on Tuesday to await arraignment, News 12 reported. Both live about half a mile from where the attack took place. They face charges including attempted murder, robbery and assault on a police officer, and are presumed innocent.

sources.title: Off-duty NYPD detective who was attacked and robbed speaks for the first time

stories.title: Soho House Plans Fourth New York Club in NoMad's Johnston Building
stories.dek: The members' club says it will open in early 2028 at Broadway and West 28th Street, anchored by a 20,000-square-foot health club.
body: Soho House plans to open its fourth New York City clubhouse in early 2028 in the Johnston Building at Broadway and West 28th Street in NoMad, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Post. The location will include the brand's first gym in the city.

The anchor will be a two-floor, 20,000-square-foot Soho Health Club with saunas, ice baths, a hammam, instructor-led classes and a smoothie counter, according to the report. Other planned spaces include a club bar, a drawing room overlooking Broadway, a terrace and a live performance space.

The 12-story Beaux-Arts building, completed in 1903, sits in the landmarked Madison Square North Historic District. It already houses The Ned NoMad hotel, which will keep 120 rooms on floors five through 12, while Soho House reworks the first four floors for members. The two brands will have separate entrances, and there will be no bundled pricing, the Post reported.

A company spokeswoman said New York members have long asked for gym and wellness facilities. The company has said its three existing city locations, in the Meatpacking District, on the Lower East Side and in DUMBO, could not fit a fitness operation of this size. Membership costs $6,000 at each New York location and includes access to the brand's other houses.

Hoodline noted that Soho House froze new member admissions in New York, London and Los Angeles for 2024 amid complaints about overcrowding, according to The Points Guy. Details on the build-out are expected closer to the opening.

sources.title: Soho House Plans Fourth NYC Club in NoMad's Johnston Building by 2028

stories.title: Mamdani Launches 'Debt Demolisher' Relief Program for Unpaid City Fines
stories.dek: A temporary program running through Jan. 10, 2027, lets residents settle certain unpaid city fines at a discount, with interest waived.
body: New York City has launched a temporary program that lets residents settle certain unpaid city fines at a discount, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Tuesday, NY1 reported. The program, called the Debt Demolisher, runs until Jan. 10, 2027.

It covers outstanding Environmental Control Board judgments stemming from unpaid violations issued by agencies including the Department of Transportation, the Department of Sanitation and the Department of Buildings, according to the city. Those violations range from building code issues to improper mattress disposal. The city expects the program to bring in about $25 million in fines it says might otherwise never be collected.

Under the terms, residents who received a default judgment for missing a hearing at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings must pay the full base fine, while the default penalty and accrued interest are waived. Those found liable after attending a hearing pay 75 percent of the imposed fine, with interest waived, NY1 reported.

Some judgments are excluded, including those entered in court after July 15, 2026, violations converted into tax liens and violations under criminal investigation. Residents can check eligibility online and submit a form with their name, address and ticket or OATH ID number.

In a statement, Mamdani said city government should not saddle New Yorkers with endless fines and interest, and that the purpose of fines is to encourage compliance with safety and health rules rather than make it harder to run a business or repair a home.

sources.title: Mamdani rolls out debt relief program for unpaid city fines

stories.title: Mamdani Orders NYPD Review of Use-of-Force Policies After Teen's Death
stories.dek: The mayor announced police accountability measures after an officer facing charges over a 2024 fatal shooting in Queens retired before his disciplinary trial.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has directed the NYPD to conduct a comprehensive review of its use-of-force policies and practices and announced several police accountability measures, according to City Hall, NY1 reported. City Hall said the review will be the first of its kind in a decade and will take place over the coming months.

The moves follow the retirement of an officer who faced disciplinary charges in the fatal police shooting of a 19-year-old in March 2024, according to the mayor's office. The officer retired before a disciplinary trial could be held. Police shot the teen at his family's home in Queens after he called 911 during a mental health crisis, NY1 reported.

The measures include a new notification system meant to ensure disciplinary cases are completed before an officer retires, and a $2.6 million funding increase for the NYPD Office of the Inspector General that City Hall said would triple the office's current headcount. The NYPD will also be formally required to notify the state Division of Criminal Justice Services and submit decertification information when an officer with pending charges retires, which the city said would keep such officers from being hired by another law enforcement agency in the state. The city will also standardize information sharing with families after critical incidents.
In a statement, Mamdani said accountability standards must be at their highest when the government uses force against a New Yorker.
NY1 said it had asked the NYPD for comment. The article did not say when the measures take effect.

sources.title: Mamdani orders NYPD to review use-of-force policies after teen's death
